samples.question: At the top of the picture is a shelf of six square slots in a row, numbered by their drawn left-to-right position. A slot either holds one coloured disc or is empty. A thick black rectangle is drawn around exactly one slot: that is the queried slot, and the ring marks a place on the shelf, never a particular disc. Below the shelf is a row of cream cards, applied one at a time in drawn left-to-right order, as the grey arrow under the row shows. Each card carries a small strip of six white boxes standing for the six shelf slots in the same left-to-right order, and a black triangle drawn just under that strip; the card acts on the slot whose white box is nearest to the triangle. Above the strip each card carries either a coloured disc or a plain grey square. A card with a coloured disc is an insert: the disc in the named slot and every disc to its right each move one slot to the right, whatever was in the sixth slot falls off the end of the shelf and is gone, and a new disc of the card's colour is placed in the named slot. A card with a grey square is a remove: whatever the named slot holds is taken away, everything to its right moves one slot to the left, and the sixth slot ends empty. Empty slots shift in exactly the same way as discs do, and a card's named slot always refers to the shelf as it stands when that card acts, not to the shelf as first drawn. The shelf is drawn only in its starting state: no later shelf, and not the final shelf, is drawn anywhere in the picture. The queried slot is guaranteed to hold a disc once every card has acted, and its colour is one of red, orange, blue or green. After every card has acted in order, what colour is the disc in the ringed slot? Answer with one word: red, orange, blue or green.
